open_points.subject: A8 run-setting presence and string decoding
open_points.text: that module decides how a value is read. A required setting that is absent ends the start, and an optional one that is absent takes its default.
open_points.question: Does “absent” mean only an unset environment variable, or also an empty or whitespace-only value, and are string settings preserved exactly or trimmed before validation and use?
options: Only an unset variable is absent; preserve every present string exactly
Treat an empty value as absent; preserve other values exactly
Trim whitespace, then treat an empty result as absent
open_points.default_guess: Only an unset variable is absent, and every present string is preserved exactly.

witness.initial: All required settings are valid; PORTAL_DELIVERER_TIMEZONE is set to the empty string.
events: The runtime settings module reads PORTAL_DELIVERER_TIMEZONE.
outcomes: The empty value counts as absent, so Europe/Madrid is used and startup continues.
The empty value is present but is not a known time zone, so startup ends.

open_points.subject: A8 port setting
open_points.text: The port is a whole number from 1 to 65535
open_points.question: Which environment-variable spellings represent a whole number: only non-empty ASCII decimal digits, or also signs, surrounding whitespace, leading zeros, Unicode digits, or other forms accepted by the chosen integer parser?
options: Only ASCII decimal digits are accepted
Any spelling accepted by the runtime integer parser is accepted
ASCII digits with surrounding whitespace or a leading plus sign are accepted
open_points.default_guess: Require non-empty ASCII decimal digits and then enforce the range 1 through 65535.

witness.initial: All settings are valid and PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT is set to +8850.
events: The runtime settings module decodes the port.
outcomes: Startup succeeds and the service uses port 8850 because the integer parser accepts a leading plus sign.
Startup ends because +8850 is not an ASCII-digits representation.

open_points.subject: A8 RuntimeEnvironment setting
open_points.text: required: the DEVELOPMENT, TEST or PRODUCTION member of = models.RuntimeEnvironment (values `development`, `test`, `production`)
open_points.question: Must PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT equal one of the three lowercase member values exactly, or may the settings module also accept member names, case variants, or surrounding whitespace?
options: Accept only the exact lowercase values
Accept both member names and values
Apply trimming and case folding before matching
open_points.default_guess: Accept only the exact lowercase values development, test, and production.

witness.initial: All other settings are valid and PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT is set to PRODUCTION.
events: The runtime settings module resolves the environment enumeration.
outcomes: Startup succeeds because PRODUCTION is the enumeration member name.
Startup ends because the setting is not the exact value production.

open_points.subject: A5 and A8 startup checks
open_points.text: At the start it is opened once; its last component is opened without following a link
open_points.question: In what order are run settings validated and startup files opened, particularly when the new environment setting is invalid at the same time as credential_file or the connections file is invalid?
options: Validate all run settings, including environment, before opening any startup file
Open and validate the credential file before validating the remaining settings
Perform startup checks in the order their modules happen to initialize
open_points.default_guess: Validate all run settings first, then open and validate the credential file and other startup files in an explicitly fixed order.

witness.initial: PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT is invalid and credential_file names a regular credential file whose opening is visible in the host's file-access audit log.
events: Startup encounters both the invalid environment and the credential-file check.
outcomes: Startup rejects the environment before opening the credential file, so the audit log contains no credential-file access.
Startup opens the credential file before rejecting the environment, so the audit log records the access.
witness.observer: the installation operator reviewing file-access auditing
